title: Absolutely Maximally Entangled States of $2q$ Parties in Every Odd Prime-Power Dimension $q$
abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states represent an extreme form of multipartite entanglement: every reduced system containing at most half of the parties is maximally mixed. These states provide perfect tensors and optimal quantum error-correcting codes, yet their existence is known only in restricted parameter regimes. For every odd prime power $q=p^e\ge3$, we construct a stabilizer $\mathrm{AME}(2q,q)$ state whose normalized one-party projection yields a stabilizer $\mathrm{AME}(2q-1,q)$ state. A closed-form $q\times q$ bordered-circulant matrix $A_q$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ generates a Hermitian self-dual maximum distance separable (MDS) code $[2q,q,q+1]_{q^2}$, which lies outside the extended Reed-Solomon classes. In suitable bases, the amplitude tensors define normalized $q$-unitary complex Hadamard matrices of order $q^q$ with $p$th-root phases. Additional constructions yield $\mathrm{AME}(q+3,q)$ states and families at intermediate particle numbers through explicit rescalings of selected submatrices. We also provide nine explicit parent matrices and the corresponding one-party projections.
summary: This paper constructs a family of Absolutely Maximally Entangled (AME) quantum states for dimensions $q$ that are odd prime powers. The construction is deeply rooted in algebraic coding theory, utilizing Hermitian self-dual MDS codes over finite fields. These states are significant because they represent extreme entanglement useful for quantum error correction and defining optimal quantum resources.
main_problem: The primary goal is the construction of Absolutely Maximally Entangled (AME) states, which represent an extreme form of multipartite entanglement.
main_result: The authors construct stabilizer AME$(2q, q)$ states for every odd prime power $q=p^e$, and derive corresponding AME$(2q-1, q)$ states.
method: The construction heavily relies on generating Hermitian self-dual Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes using bordered-circulant matrices over finite fields $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.
model_or_system: The system is a pure quantum state $|\Psiangle \in (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes N}$ defined by its entanglement properties, specifically requiring its reduced density matrix to be maximally mixed for small subsets of parties.
key_observables: The entanglement structure, quantified by the maximal mixing of reduced density matrices, and the associated quantum code parameters (e.g., $[2q, q, q+1]_{q^2}$).
important_parameters: The dimension $q$ must be an odd prime power ($q=p^e, p 	ext{ odd prime}$). The state parameters are $(N, d) = (2q, q)$ and $(2q-1, q)$.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on specific algebraic properties within finite fields ($\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$) and the existence of certain matrices satisfying specific structural equations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the existence status of AME states for various parameters, marking the newly constructed cases. Table I collects explicit examples of parent states and their one-party projections.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the AME property, linking it to MDS codes via specific matrices ($A_q$), deriving the explicit construction for $AME(2q, q)$, and then showing the reduction to $AME(2q-1, q)$ via measurement.
why_interesting: The rigorous construction of highly entangled states like AME states provides fundamental resources for quantum error correction and quantum computation, pushing the boundaries of known entanglement bounds.
